claim: Soundness, completeness (Godel 1929/30), and compactness hold for first-order logic; but first-order validity is only semi-decidable (Church, Turing 1936) and propositional satisfiability is NP-complete (Cook 1971). A checker can confirm a found proof or counter-model, but cannot promise to find one or to halt on every input.
agent_test: Give the verifier a hard step budget; count items where it times out and check the agent reports 'undecided' rather than 'consistent'.

claim: LLM one-step deduction is mostly valid; the weak point is proof planning (choosing which valid step to take) and chain length.
agent_test: On multi-hop rule sets, compare free chain of thought with a forced 'list all derivable facts first, then pick' step at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Accuracy on logical deduction falls with the number of reasoning steps (Multi-LogiEval d1 to d5: propositional mean 85.4 to 43.0, first-order 83.2 to 33.0; ProverQA GPT-4o CoT easy 94.2, medium 79.4, hard 50.0).
agent_test: Plot agent accuracy by proof depth with and without the schema at equal tokens; the schema should flatten the slope.

claim: Premise order changes accuracy though entailment is unchanged: forward (proof) order is best; permuting costs 20-30 points for GPT-4-turbo and PaLM 2-L, over 40 for Gemini 1.0 Pro and GPT-3.5 (older models).
agent_test: Add a 'restate premises in dependency order' step and compare with raw order on shuffled-premise items.

claim: Under bad premise order the commonest error is fact hallucination (inventing an unproven fact to close a step), not a wrong rule.
agent_test: Have the verifier tag each step 'given / derived from which lines'; count steps with no source line.

claim: Irrelevant premises cost accuracy on hard first-order items: GPT-4o CoT hard 50.0 rises to 57.4 without distractors and 62.4 when also ordered.
agent_test: Add a relevance-filter pass; measure on hard-tier items.

claim: Chain-of-thought gain over standard prompting shrinks as difficulty rises (ProverQA mean gain +12.9 easy, +8.4 medium, +3.9 hard; FOLIO +5.4).
agent_test: Check whether extra tokens help on hard items or whether search or verification is needed instead.

claim: LLM translation to first-order logic is syntactically valid far more often than semantically correct: FOLIO GPT-4 few-shot validity 93.9 vs execution accuracy 63.8; zero-shot 86.1 vs 51.7.
agent_test: Measure how often an agent's formalised rule set yields the labelled answer; require the formal form to be read back in English and compared.

claim: Translate-then-solve (Logic-LM, LINC, SatLM, Faithful CoT) beats standard prompting and often CoT where reasoning is search-like (GPT-4 ProofWriter standard 52.7, CoT 68.1, Logic-LM 79.7; SatLM ProofWriter 99.7 vs CoT 80.1).
agent_test: Offer the agent a solver call and compare with pure CoT at equal tokens on proof-search items.

claim: The solver route does not always win: on FOLIO GPT-4 LINC 72.5 vs CoT 75.3 (McNemar p=0.58); on PrOntoQA GPT-4 CoT 98.79 beats Logic-LM 83.20. Gains concentrate in weaker models and deep proofs.
agent_test: Route by item: use the solver only where CoT samples disagree or depth is high; test the router.

claim: Solver and CoT fail in different ways (LINC loses information in translation; CoT states conclusions that contradict its own steps), so they are partly complementary.
agent_test: Run both, flag disagreements for a third look; measure the oracle-union accuracy.

claim: Repair loops that feed solver errors back raise executability (Logic-LM FOLIO GPT-4 79.9 to 85.8, GPT-3.5 66.7 to 84.3), but repair can fix syntax while adding meaning errors (Logic-LM++ mixed: GPT-3.5 FOLIO 62.80 to 62.25). New: VeriCoT solver-guided reflection raised pass rate by 8 to 15 points but task accuracy moved -1.7 (ProofWriter), +0.6 (BioASQ), +1.4 (SARA); Logic-LM++ pairwise semantic check +5.9 on GPT-4 FOLIO (78.92 to 84.80), -0.55 on GPT-3.5.
agent_test: Count repairs that keep syntax valid but change the English meaning; require a back-translation check after each repair.

claim: Solver signals UNSAT (contradictory spec) and AMBIG (under-determined spec) can be used to abstain; selective accuracy on GSM-Sys is 77% vs 45% for program-aided, at lower coverage. New: with a real SMT verifier (VeriCoT) only 15 to 45% of chains verify, precision 84 to 94%; a prompt-only verifier (SymbCoT) removes unfaithful-correct answers (6% to 0% in a small manual check) at about 30% extra output tokens, and reports no abstain coverage.
agent_test: Make 'rules contradict' and 'underdetermined' explicit outputs; measure selective accuracy vs coverage.

claim: Benchmarks can be partly answered from world knowledge, inflating logic scores: JustLogic (random truth values) shows prior-knowledge gaps in FOLIO and LogiQA 2.0; removing universal rules from 60 ProverQA items drops GPT-4o CoT from 68.3 to 45.0.
agent_test: Evaluate on counterfactual or nonsense-content versions; a drop signals content-driven answers.

claim: Reasoning models reach or pass the human average on JustLogic (R1 80.9, o1 72.9 vs human 73.0, ceiling 100; GPT-4o 65.6) but degrade on large search spaces (ZebraLogic X-Large: o1-full 42.5). New: DeepSeek-R1 CoT scores 86.2 on FOLIO (JustLogic side table), above the 2023 GPT-4 solver pipelines (Logic-LM 78.92); reasoning-model scores differ widely by model (Knights and Knaves: o3-mini-high 0.94, R1 0.81, o1 0.42).
agent_test: Compare the schema on a non-reasoning model against a reasoning-model baseline at equal tokens.

claim: Models, like people, are more accurate when the conclusion is believable (belief bias). In people the effect is large (Evans et al. 1983, opened: N=24 Exp 1, percent accepting valid-believable 92, valid-unbelievable 46, invalid-believable 92, invalid-unbelievable 8; Exp 2 N=64: 88/56/72/13; Exp 3 N=32: 91/53/67/6).
agent_test: Ask for validity with neutral, believable-false and believable-true content; require the agent to judge form first.

claim: Rule type matters: GPT-4 is near 100 on hypothetical syllogism but about 59 (Yes-class) on modus tollens; negation and implicit-premise rules are hard. Yes-label accuracy is far below binary-QA average (ChatGPT 48.0 vs 81.9; GPT-4 64.0 vs 89.6).
agent_test: Add a contrapositive and negation check step and measure on modus tollens and negation items.

claim: Large LLMs break negation and implication consistency on simple facts; a semantic-loss fine-tune improves it. This is a training result, not a scaffold result.
agent_test: Check the agent's stored claims pairwise for p and not-p, and p implies q, before use.

claim: Weakness-targeted examples (LogicAsker) raise rule accuracy by about 5 points (GPT-4o 91.9 to 97.2); failure rates across six LLMs were 29% to 90%.
agent_test: Not a scaffold test; skip unless a few-shot rule library is added.

claim: Fully LLM-based pipelines with a verifier (SymbCoT) beat CoT by +6.1 (GPT-3.5) and +9.3 (GPT-4) on average, with each module contributing; no external prover needed.
agent_test: Ablate the verifier step at equal tokens.

claim: Fine-tuning on solver traces (LoGiPT) or prover-generated data (ProverQA +21 to +44 points) raises accuracy; parse failure is the stated motivation (CodeLlama-13B-Base parse success 0.33% on ProofWriter).
agent_test: Training result; outside the scaffold-only scope.

claim: Human belief bias: acceptance of conclusions is strongly driven by believability (Evans et al. 1983, three experiments, opened). A 22-study hierarchical-Bayesian ROC meta-analysis (Trippas et al. 2018, N=993, opened) finds believability does not change discriminability on average, supporting the response-bias account, but individual differences moderate it. Dube et al. 2010 itself was not opened.
agent_test: In a verify step, report false-accept and false-reject rates separately by whether the conclusion sounds true; do not treat one accuracy number as the measure of reasoning.

claim: Frontier reasoning models can usually tell that a small natural-language rule set is inconsistent (SATBench easy UNSAT: o4-mini 98.2, R1 98.2) but degrade as it grows (hard UNSAT: o4-mini 65.0, R1 83.6, DeepSeek-V3 74.3, Claude-3.7 42.1, GPT-4o 18.9) and weaker models default to saying satisfiable (hard SAT 66.7 vs UNSAT 39.3 averaged over 20 models).
agent_test: Seed a rule set with one hidden conflict at 10, 30 and 50 rules; measure detection rate with and without a required clause-by-clause assignment.

claim: Naming which rules conflict (minimal unsatisfiable subset) is harder than detecting that a conflict exists: on SATQuest, MUS and MCS tasks were the lowest-accuracy class for all models (o3-mini overall 0.56, R1 0.42, GPT-4.1 0.38), and o3-mini shortened its reasoning and invented shortcuts at high complexity.
agent_test: Ask for the smallest conflicting subset and check it by pairwise test; compare to a free-form answer.

claim: A correct SAT or UNSAT label does not mean a valid trace: judged trace validity was 10 to 30 points lower than label accuracy on SAT (o4-mini 94.7 vs 74.6; Claude-3.7 83.2 vs 47.4). Dominant errors: satisfiability bias (o4-mini 68.7%), context inconsistency (R1 44.7%), condition omission (about 13%).
agent_test: Require an explicit assignment and check every clause; log omitted conditions.

claim: Back-translation style checks have mixed value: SATBench found 97 of 100 clause translations faithful after a solver equivalence filter; Logic-LM++'s pairwise semantic check helped GPT-4 (+5.9 FOLIO) but not GPT-3.5; LLM-written semantic tests gave +6.6 (LLM-ARC 8-shot); VeriCoT reflection left translation errors unchanged. No source measured how often back-translation catches a meaning error at equal tokens.
agent_test: Plant 20 meaning-changing translation errors; measure catch rate of a back-translate-and-compare step and its token cost.

claim: Bounded counter-model search (premises plus negated conclusion satisfiable) beat LLM judgement of the same formal forms on fallacy detection (F1 0.78 vs 0.66 LOGIC; 0.80 vs 0.73 LogicClimate), but end-to-end GPT-4o (0.96) and o1-preview (0.93) beat the pipeline on the familiar LOGIC set; 54% of pipeline errors were missing background knowledge. Counter-model versus proof search was not tested.
agent_test: On invalid-conclusion items, compare a prompt that builds a small counter-model with one that attempts a proof, at equal tokens.

claim: Selecting among samples is the bottleneck, not generating a correct one: on ZebraLogic GPT-4o best-of-32 with an oracle reaches 60.3 (128: 69.1) while majority vote gives 38.0 and a reward model 34.8 against a 31.7 baseline. No study tested using sample disagreement to decide when to call a solver.
agent_test: Measure whether disagreement among 5 CoT samples predicts CoT error; if so, gate the solver on it.

claim: Distractors still hurt reasoning models: appended irrelevant text raised R1 error from 1.5% to 4.5% on math (3x) and lengthened outputs by 1.5x or more in 17% to 42% of cases across o1, o3-mini, R1. Premise-order effects in 2025-2026 reasoning models are unmeasured in the sources found.
agent_test: Run the premise-order permutation test on a reasoning model; test a restate-in-dependency-order step at equal tokens.

claim: Contraposition expansion is weakly supported: Logic-of-Thought removal of the contraposition step cost 3.8 points on a 135-item FOLIO subset (76.00 to 72.22) in a bundled ablation, with GPT-4 gain from the whole method only +0.6. Modus tollens stays harder than other forms in JustLogic even for reasoning models. No test of a standalone contrapositive step on reasoning models.
agent_test: Add a one-line contrapositive of each rule; measure modus tollens items only.

claim: Answer accuracy and reasoning soundness diverge: outcome-reward RL on ProverQA gave 91.3% Hard accuracy with 22.0% sound chains; formal step verification raised soundness to 76.1% at equal accuracy (92.97). Unsound chains do not improve with more majority votes.
agent_test: Judge chains for soundness, not only answers, when comparing scaffolds.
